## Claim check (abstract hypotheses; rules fixed in scripts/render_summary.py)

| Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Physics-constrained diffusion is sharper than the deterministic baseline (closer to observed sharpness) | **supported** | grad ratio 1.42 vs 0.68; HF ratio 1.25 vs 0.70 (1 = observed) |
| Physics-constrained diffusion is sharper than unconstrained diffusion (closer to observed sharpness) | **not supported** | grad ratio 1.42 vs 1.41; HF ratio 1.25 vs 1.11 (1 = observed) |
| Physics constraints make forecasts more physically consistent | **supported** | envelope / monotone violation fraction diff_phys+G+P 0.029 / 0.025, diff_phys 0.031 / 0.024, diff_plain 0.056 / 0.089, det 0.018 / 0.214; monotone violations are scored with the same stress perturbation used in the training loss (in-sample for the physics models); observations themselves: envelope 0.035, rate 0.022 (fewer violations than observed = over-constraint, not physics) |
| Physics-constrained diffusion is more accurate (CRPS) than the baselines | **partly supported** | vs clim_anomaly: diff -0.0762 [-0.1008, -0.0560]; vs climatology: diff -0.0426 [-0.0652, -0.0248]; vs det: diff -0.0214 [-0.0248, -0.0173]; vs diff_plain: diff 0.0034 [0.0000, 0.0071]; vs persistence: diff -0.0519 [-0.0676, -0.0369] (negative = proposed better); MAE: vs climatology: -0.0109 [-0.0298, 0.0041]; vs det: 0.0103 [0.0059, 0.0166]; vs diff_plain: 0.0054 [0.0004, 0.0110]; vs persistence: -0.0203 [-0.0333, -0.0071]. CRPS of a single deterministic forecast equals its MAE, so CRPS gains over point baselines partly reflect being an ensemble; physics constraints cost accuracy relative to unconstrained diffusion where that difference is positive. Source: results/test/paired_tests.csv |
| Ensemble uncertainty is calibrated (uncertainty-aware estimates) | **not supported (overconfident: intervals too narrow)** | 90 % coverage 0.716, 50 % coverage 0.397, spread-skill 0.89 |

## Statistical caveats

- 12 test locations: bootstrap intervals over so few location clusters are likely too narrow; p-values are from 1000 bootstrap draws (0.000 means < 0.001) and are not corrected for multiple comparisons.
- **No conclusion about drought effects is solid yet**: the drought-labelled test sample is far too small (counts above).

Not tested: semi-synthetic oracle (cut by project owner's instruction: no synthetic data). Classifier-free guidance ablation (not run, see PROGRESS.md).

Limitations: see docs/LIMITATIONS.md. The drought effect is a model-based estimate, not ground truth.
